kind: post-build adversarial checkpoint (AGENT_CONTRACT section 1: what was built, what the evidence is, what the build taught us that the plan did not know)

src/control/heavy-lease.mjs: isStoreHost(raw): the syntactic host predicate. Accepts a bracketed IPv6 literal, an IPv4 literal with every octet <= 255, the single name `localhost`, and a DNS name of >= 2 labels each 1-63 chars of [a-z0-9_-] starting and ending alphanumeric, total <= 253, one trailing dot stripped. Everything else is not a store.

neonEndpointKey(raw): for a host under .neon.tech whose FIRST label starts `ep-` and ends `-pooler`, returns the direct spelling; otherwise returns the host unchanged. NEON_HOST_SUFFIX is exported so the scope of the strip is a named constant, not a literal buried in a branch.

canonicalStoreKey(raw): now resolves the host in both branches (scheme'd URL, and bare with userinfo/path/port stripped), lowercases it, strips one trailing dot, then REFUSES unless isStoreHost, and finally returns neonEndpointKey(host). A refused spelling throws LEASE_STORE_INVALID quoting the caller's original string in the message and carrying it as err.store.

The module header gains the P-307 paragraph: the two checks, why the key must BE a host, that the pooler strip is about CONTENTION IDENTITY and that connecting with a -pooler URL is still refused by refusePoolerHost in src/db/connect.mjs.

the race: takeHeavyScanLease still does INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + read-back + a recorded refusal row
src/db/connect.mjs and refusePoolerHost -- connect-time behaviour is untouched; this lane changes the KEY, not the connection

theRuleChosen.differsFromCp1: No. CP1 chose REFUSE (no alias table) for item 1 and UNIFY for item 2; both are what shipped, and the reasoning in CP1 is the reasoning at close.
theRuleChosen.theOneRule: The contention key is a host, or nothing is keyed. Applied in BOTH the URL branch and the bare branch, so prepending a scheme cannot smuggle a label back into a private namespace -- CP1 did not name that door explicitly and a reviewer would have found it: `--store postgres://factory-store` would otherwise have keyed `factory-store`.
theRuleChosen.whySyntacticAndNotABlacklist: measured, per item 3 -- see the census. `p281-probe.invalid` is a host (>= 2 labels) that the fleet really leased, and two shipped suites lease `.invalid` names; a reserved-TLD rule would refuse names the fleet uses today, which item 3 forbids.

1_factory_store_and_the_host_cannot_both.evidence: PASS. The refused spelling throws inside normalizeSpec, before BEGIN: the test asserts the recording client saw ZERO calls (not even BEGIN), so a refused spelling cannot leave a row. Both orders are covered; the loud direction (a caller through the factory host's URL vs a caller naming `factory-store`) is a second test and cannot produce two takes.

2_a_different_real_host_still_takes.evidence: PASS (unit, on a doubled client) and PASS against the real index (p281-heavy-lease-live: two hosts, two live rows, zero refusals).

3_revert_fails_test_1.test: P-307 falsifier 3: the refusal is the check, not the surrounding code (revert fails test 1)
3_revert_fails_test_1.evidence: PASS, two-sided. (a) The source is asserted to contain the call site `if (!isStoreHost(host)) {` and `return neonEndpointKey(host);`, so deleting the check fails this test even if someone edits the other tests' expectations. (b) A temporary copy of the module with that call site replaced by `if (false) {` is imported and asserted to return `factory-store` from canonicalStoreKey -- the pre-P-307 behaviour, which is exactly what test 1 catches. The copy also still refuses the empty string, so the probe isolates the check rather than the whole function. The probe file is written under src/control with a pid suffix and removed in a finally; `git status` after the suite is clean.

4_the_existing_doors_still_contend.evidence: PASS. item2_both_orders_plus_a_different_endpo.test: P-307 item 2 falsifier 4: the Neon pooler and direct hostnames are ONE key, in both orders -- and, live, on the REAL partial unique index

whatTheBuildTaughtThatThePlanDidNot: FIVE SHIPPED TESTS FAILED ON THE NEW RULE, and none of them was about the store key. Three test files carried PLACEHOLDER DSNs whose host was a single label: `postgres://x` (test/parcel-envelope-cells.test.mjs x3 and test/parcel-setback-cells.test.mjs x3) and `postgres://fixture/staging_*` (test/publish.test.mjs). They are placeholders for 'some DSN' in tests about city scope, the laptop write freeze, and tier-2 baking. CP1 pre-registered the rule's consequence for FLEET hosts and checked the module's consumers, but did not look for single-label hosts inside the TEST SUITE, so this was discovered by running the suite, not predicted.

THE FIX: the placeholder now has a host in it -- `postgres://x.invalid/neondb` and `postgres://fixture.invalid/staging_*`. No assertion changed, no test renamed, and the two files are otherwise untouched. The full suite after the change has no new failure (below). This is recorded rather than glossed because 'I edited five tests to make my rule pass' is a sentence that must come with its evidence, and the evidence is: the edited strings are DSNs in tests that never read a store key, the change is to the host only, and the census proves no fleet host is refused.

A REFUSAL IS ONLY USEFUL IF IT CANNOT BE MISTAKEN FOR A CRASH. The 2026-09-17 session's client run ended `{"code":"FAILED","message":"fetch failed"}` on exit 1 -- the same exit code a 400 LEASE_STORE_INVALID would have produced through the old client mapping. That is why the doc_repo client diff gives the code its own exit (7) and prints the factory's reason, and why the live/API tests assert the 400 body's `message` quotes the spelling rather than only its `error`.

THE FULL SUITE IS NOT HERMETIC ACROSS FILES ON ONE DATABASE. test/p284-stage-run-records-live.test.mjs fails when the whole suite runs concurrently against one scratch store (`the view must emit the same pair: 15 !== 1`) and passes when run alone -- it counts rows for a county pair other live files also write. Proven environmental, not this lane: the identical full run with this change STASHED fails at the same site. Both runs are on a freshly created database, and the pre-existing LDT-pin and OPS-21 failures appear in both.

`--store postgres://factory-store` WAS A REAL HOLE IN THE CP1 RULE AS FIRST WRITTEN. Refusing only the bare form would have left the same defect reachable by typing a scheme. The rule is applied to both branches as a result; CP1's text is amended by this note rather than quietly fixed.

clientDiffHandback.patch: _inbox/2026-09-17_p307-lease-key-is-a-host_client.patch (git apply -p1 from the doc_repo root; verified to apply cleanly to the worktree's copy with `git apply --check`, exit 0, and the applied result runs its selftest green: 36 checks, PASS)
what: LEASE_STORE_INVALID is a named export and gets its own exit code, 7, next free. Explicitly NOT 1: exit 1 is this script's crash/transport bucket and the 2026-09-17 `fetch failed` used it.

outcomeFor now returns the factory's `reason` (the body's message) with every refusal and for any 400, and a 400 whose error is LEASE_STORE_INVALID maps to that code -- while a 400 with any other error still keeps its own name (asserted both directions, so the mapping cannot silently widen).
The header documents the rule and the exit code, and states that this script does NOT re-implement the host rule: a second copy of a key rule in another repo drifts from the first.
The selftest's `checks` count is now COUNTED rather than the hardcoded 24, which had drifted the moment anything was added.
clientDiffHandback.e2eVerification: Lane-local harness (P:/tmp/p307-scratch/p307_client_e2e.mjs, scratch only) ran the PATCHED client against a REAL createControlServer on the scratch database. Results: `--store factory-store` -> exit 7, code LEASE_STORE_INVALID, reason quoting the spelling, HTTP 400, no lease row; `--store <direct host>` -> exit 0, 201, store = the host; the POOLER spelling of that same endpoint -> exit 5 LEASE_HELD, reason 'store ep-p307-....neon.tech is held by ...', i.e. the direct key; a different host -> exit 0; the URL form with the host UPPERCASED -> exit 5 LEASE_HELD on the direct key. Both taken rows were then released through the client's own release verb (200, released_at set).

remainsOpen: factory-control must be DEPLOYED with this revision before any live refusal can be observed; until then a live take on `factory-store` still succeeds (the API on the deployed revision does not carry isStoreHost).

The historical `factory-store` rows stay in the table: this lane writes no lease data. A reader should expect them in the census after deploy, and they are the evidence that the defect was live rather than theoretical.

The one live caller that has been typing the label is p266p268-lane; after deploy its next take on `factory-store` gets 400 LEASE_STORE_INVALID naming the spelling. That is the intended, loud outcome, and the integrator should expect it rather than treat it as a regression.
